Jio IPO Receives Strong Response: Issue Gets 3.2x Subscription On Day 1, QIB Portion Booked 9.4x

Reported By :
  • Business Desk
  • ,News18.com
Last Updated:October 22, 2026, 07:47 IST

The Jio Platforms IPO sees strong demand from institutional investors, with the qualified institutional buyers (QIB) portion booked 9.42 times the shares reserved for the category.

Jio Platforms IPO: The Rs 30,213-crore initial public offering (IPO) of Jio Platforms Ltd, the telecom and digital arm of Reliance Industries, received a strong response from investors on the first day of bidding on Wednesday, October 21, with the issue subscribed 3.2 times overall. The issue saw a strong demand from institutional investors, with the qualified institutional buyers (QIB) portion booked 9.42 times the shares reserved for the category.

The IPO, the largest public issue in India’s capital market history, crossed the full-subscription mark within around 100 minutes of opening for bidding, making it the fastest among mega-IPOs to reach full subscription.

Recommended Stories
  1. Jio Platforms IPO Creates History: ₹30,213 Crore Issue Subscribed in 100 Minutes | Business News
  2. Jio IPO Creates Record: Issue Fully Subscribed In Less Than 100 Minutes, QIB Booked 3.25x; Fastest Among Mega IPOs
  3. Jio Platforms IPO: How Digital Giant Built A Rs 1.47 Lakh Crore Revenue Engine In 10 Years
  4. Jio Platforms IPO, Paras Healthcare Issue To Keep Primary Market Busy In Holiday-Shortened Week

Demand extended across investor categories, with the non-institutional investor (NII) segment, employee quota and shareholder reservation portion also receiving bids exceeding their respective allocations.

Jio Platforms IPO Subscription Status: Records Set

The QIB category led the demand on Day 1, with bids for 9.42 times the shares reserved for institutional investors. The NII portion was subscribed 1.83 times, while the employee quota received bids for 1.36 times its allocation. The shareholder reservation portion was subscribed 1.46 times.

advertisement

The retail investor segment attracted bids worth more than Rs 6,900 crore, marking the highest Day 1 retail demand for an IPO in India.

Overall, the issue received bids amounting to around 3.2 times the shares on offer, reflecting strong demand despite the size of the offering.

Jio Platforms IPO Draws Strong Institutional Demand

Timeline

Jio Platforms IPO

Jio Platforms Ltd, the digital services and telecom arm of Reliance Industries, has advanced its initial public offering (IPO) process toward a historic market debut. Following board approval of the Draft Red Herring Prospectus for a fresh issue of up to 27 crore equity shares during the 49th Annual General Meeting, SEBI issued its final observations in August 2026. Ahead of its scheduled subscription window, the company attracted over $20 billion in institutional bids and finalized its share price band at Rs 1,065-1,119 to raise up to Rs 30,213 crore, setting the stage for India's largest-ever IPO opening from October 21 to October 23, 2026.

Institutional investors emerged as the key drivers of the IPO’s strong opening-day performance. The robust QIB subscription followed significant demand during the anchor investor allocation, which reportedly attracted bids exceeding 30 times the shares available.

The anchor book saw participation from global sovereign wealth funds, pension funds and domestic mutual funds.

The strong institutional response is a key indicator of investor interest in Jio Platforms’ digital services business and its growth prospects. However, subscription figures reflect demand for shares and do not guarantee listing gains.

Jio Platforms IPO Compared With Previous Mega-Issues

Jio Platforms’ rapid subscription surpasses the opening-day performance of several large Indian IPOs.

The Rs 30,213-crore issue reached full subscription within around 100 minutes of opening. Bajaj Housing Finance’s IPO crossed full subscription by around 2 pm on its first day, while LG Electronics India’s IPO reached full subscription by the end of Day 1.

Hyundai Motor India’s IPO, which had been India’s largest IPO before the Jio Platforms issue, was subscribed around 18% by the end of its first day.

Fresh Issue: Where Will the IPO Proceeds Go?

Unlike Hyundai Motor India and LG Electronics India, whose IPOs were entirely offers for sale (OFS), Jio Platforms’ offering is structured as a fresh issue of 27 crore shares.

In an OFS, proceeds go to the selling shareholders. In a fresh issue, the company receives the proceeds to fund its business requirements.

The funds raised through Jio Platforms’ IPO are expected to strengthen its financial position and

support
its growth plans across digital connectivity, cloud infrastructure and artificial intelligence-related enterprise services.

Advertisement

Jio Platforms IPO: Key Dates

The IPO is scheduled to close on Friday, October 23, 2026. The basis of allotment is expected to be finalised on Monday, October 26, followed by the credit of shares to demat accounts on Tuesday, October 27.

The qualified institutional buyers portion was booked 9.42 times, while the retail investor segment attracted bids worth over Rs 6,900 crore, setting a record for the highest Day 1 retail demand for an Indian IPO. Other segments like the non-institutional investor portion, employee quota, and shareholder reservation also exceeded their allocations.

The Jio Platforms IPO closes on Friday, October 23, 2026. The basis of allotment will be finalised on Monday, October 26, and shares will be credited to demat accounts on Tuesday, October 27, before listing on the BSE and NSE on Wednesday, October 28, 2026.

Barclays Layoffs: UK-Based Bank Slashing 5,000 Jobs, Nearly 5% Workforce, Amid AI Push

Published By :
  • Business Desk
  • ,News18.com
Last Updated:October 22, 2026, 15:44 IST

Barclays has already eliminated around 1,000 positions, with the remaining job cuts expected to be completed by the end of 2026.

Got Question about the News?

Barclays Layoffs 2026: Barclays is cutting 5,000 jobs, nearly 5% of its global workforce, as the UK-based banking major steps up efforts to reduce costs, improve operational efficiency and harness artificial intelligence (AI) across its business, according to reports.

The bank has already eliminated around 1,000 positions, with the remaining job cuts expected to be completed by the end of 2026. Most of the job losses are likely to be concentrated in the UK, Barclays’ home market, and will primarily affect operational and functional roles. However, the restructuring will have a global impact.

Recommended Stories
  1. Jio IPO Day 2: Subscription At 3.27x On Strong Institutional Interest, QIB Demand At 9.42x; GMP At 22%
  2. Jio Platforms IPO: How Investors Can Improve Their Allotment Chances Through Eligible Quotas
  3. Jio IPO Day 2 Live Updates: Subscription Hits 4.38x, QIB Portion Crosses 10x; GMP At Nearly 22%
  4. Jio IPO Receives Strong Response: Issue Gets 3.2x Subscription On Day 1, QIB Portion Booked 9.4x

The move reflects a broader shift across the financial services industry, where banks are increasingly investing in technology and AI-driven processes to streamline operations and reduce their reliance on human intervention in certain functions.

According to Sky News, Barclays Group Chief Executive C S Venkatakrishnan said the job reductions were linked to technology investments made over several years, adding that the bank would continue to invest in modernising its infrastructure to improve efficiency.

He said AI was becoming an important part of this transition and could play a bigger role in the future. However, he emphasised that the technology alone would not deliver the desired benefits without the necessary infrastructure.

Venkatakrishnan described AI as the “icing on the cake", rather than the cake itself, underscoring the importance of building modern technology systems before businesses can fully benefit from AI adoption.

The bank has been applying AI in areas where its technology infrastructure is sufficiently modern, indicating that its efficiency drive is tied to a broader digital transformation strategy rather than AI deployment alone.

Despite the planned job cuts, Barclays said it remained committed to developing employees’ skills and preparing its workforce for changing business requirements.

A bank spokesperson said Barclays was positioning itself for the future by building the workforce and capabilities required to deliver its strategy and respond to the evolving needs of customers and clients.

The spokesperson added that the bank aimed to help employees develop rewarding careers while ensuring it remained competitive in the years ahead.

However, the planned reductions underline the challenges facing employees as financial institutions reorganise their operations around technology-led business models.

Barclays’ decision comes amid a wider restructuring trend in the global banking sector, where financial institutions are examining how automation and AI can change staffing requirements, particularly in back-office operations and other functions.

Standard Chartered has also indicated that it needs to replace what its leadership described as “lower-value human capital", alongside plans for thousands of job losses.

Such moves highlight how banks are seeking to improve productivity and profitability through a combination of technology investments, operational restructuring and workforce rationalisation.

While AI adoption is expected to change the nature of several banking roles, the pace and scale of its impact will depend on how quickly institutions upgrade their systems and integrate the technology into their operations.

The job cuts were disclosed as Barclays reported third-quarter profits of £2.3 billion, marking a 12% increase from the corresponding period last year.

However, the result fell short of analysts’ expectations, with weaker-than-anticipated performance in its fixed-income trading business weighing on the outcome.

Barclays shares fell more than 2.5% following the results, as investors assessed the bank’s earnings performance and outlook.

The combination of rising profits, missed market expectations and continued cost-cutting efforts highlights the pressure on major banks to improve returns while adapting their business models to technological change.

Actor Sonu Sood has leased out a commercial unit in Versova, Andheri West, Mumbai, in a transaction registered in October 2026, according to property registration documents. The five-year rental agreement has a total rental value of around Rs 3.52 crore, according to Square Yards, citing documents available on the Maharashtra Inspector General of Registration (IGR) website.

According to the registration documents, the property is located in Aram Nagar, Versova, Andheri West. The monthly rent for the first year is Rs 5 lakh, which will increase to Rs 5.4 lakh in the second year, Rs 5.83 lakh in the third year, Rs 6.29 lakh in the fourth year and Rs 6.8 lakh in the fifth year. The agreement provides for an annual rental escalation of about 8%.

The transaction involved a security deposit of Rs 32 lakh, stamp duty of Rs 93,000 and registration charges of Rs 1,000, according to Square Yards.

Versova is a prominent residential and commercial locality in Mumbai’s western suburbs, offering connectivity to business districts and entertainment hubs across the city. The area is accessible via Link Road, SV Road and the Western Express Highway, while Versova Metro station and Andheri railway station provide access to other parts of Mumbai.

The locality also offers proximity to commercial centres such as Andheri East, Goregaon and Bandra-Kurla Complex (BKC), alongside restaurants, cafes, retail outlets, educational institutions and healthcare facilities. Its coastal setting, established social infrastructure and connectivity have helped make it a sought-after residential destination.

Sonu Sood is an Indian actor and film producer who has worked across Hindi, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada cinema. He made his acting debut with the Tamil film Kallazhagar in 1999 and subsequently appeared in films such as Yuva, Aashiq Banaya Aapne, Jodhaa Akbar, Dabangg and Simmba.

Apart from his film career, Sood gained widespread recognition for his humanitarian work during the COVID-19 pandemic, when he helped stranded migrant workers and students return home and supported people facing difficulties.

Through the Sood Charity Foundation, he has continued to support initiatives in education, healthcare and social welfare. In 2020, he received the United Nations Development Programme’s SDG Special Humanitarian Action Award for his humanitarian efforts.
